t: You're looking at the Novello Theatre, a West End theatre on Aldwych in the City of Westminster. For much of its life it was the Strand Theatre, a name it carried from 1913 until 2005. It was designed by W. G. R. Sprague, who was apprenticed to the great theatre architect Frank Matcham before setting up his own practice. Sprague went on to design at least thirty-five theatres between 1890 and 1929. Of his surviving London theatres, eleven are listed, and this is one of the places that shows his craft.
